newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli army warns Hizbollah on fire from villages.
newsitem.headline: Israeli army warns Hizbollah on fire from villages.

text.p: An Israeli general warned Lebanese Hizbollah guerrillas on Wednesday that Israel would retaliate if they ignored a ban against rocketing or shelling Israeli forces from villages in south Lebanon.

"I hope that they will continue to respect the understandings on fire from within villages and I warn and clarify that we will need to exercise self-defence for residents of the north and Israeli soldiers," Brigadier General Yomtov Samia said on Israel's army radio.
"The issue of the understandings it appears will be pushed aside. Self-defence takes precedence over any category," he said.
His comments came hours after Israeli security sources said mortars or rockets fired from Lebanon landed inside Israel's northern border.
Israeli troops were checking the area after the attack around 2 a.m. on Wednesday (2300 GMT on Tuesday). Security sources said shells fell in the Galilee panhandle region.

Israel and Hizbollah undertook not to fire on civilian targets under the 1996 ceasefire understanding which ended 17 days of an Israeli onslaught on Lebanon in which about 200 people -- mainly Lebanese civilians -- were killed.
Hizbollah also undertook not to launch attacks from within Lebanese villages.
Prosper Azran, mayor of the northern Galilee town of Kiryat Shmona, said Wednesday's shelling was "with complete certainty" directed at civilian areas.
He told Israel's army radio that residents sensed an increase in tension on the Israel-Lebanon border and were preparing bomb shelters, although they were not under army orders to do so.
"These are orders of the heart and of experience," Azran said. "I remember many days like this in the past year."
On Tuesday, Hizbollah guerrillas in south Lebanon fired a Katyusha rocket into northern Israel in retaliation for Israeli shelling that killed two Lebanese civilians in south Lebanon on Monday.

Other rockets were fired at targets inside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone. One hit a farm near an Israeli-allied South Lebanon Army militia outpost, injuring a farmer and his 15-year-old son, militia sources said.
Several mortars and rockets have been fired by the pro-Iranian Hizbollah this month, most apparently aimed at Israeli troops patrolling the south Lebanon occupation zone.
"The Katyusha rocketing was in response for the continued violation of an April 1996 understanding which bans firing on civilians," a Hizbollah spokesman told Reuters in Beirut on Tuesday.

Israeli shelling on Monday night killed two civilians in the village of Berti, east of the southern port city of Sidon, security sources said. The shelling came after two SLA militiamen were wounded in a Hizbollah rocket attack on their outpost.
Israel carved out its south Lebanon occupation zone in 1985 to protect its northern border after withdrawing the bulk of a force which invaded Lebanon in 1982.
Hizbollah is fighting a guerrilla war to oust Israeli troops from south Lebanon.
